scorecard.name: Empathy & Acknowledgment Statement
scorecard.coaching: When Malgorzata explained at [00:10] and [00:38] that the double direct debit pushed her into an unauthorized overdraft, you moved straight into ledger checks without once apologizing or acknowledging her distress.

scorecard.name: Paraphrasing
scorecard.coaching: At [00:23], you repeated the customer's exact words verbatim ('You were charged twice on your direct debit after upgrading from Fibre 150 to Fibre 500') instead of paraphrasing the issue in your own words and checking understanding.

scorecard.name: Confirmed the issue is resolved
scorecard.coaching: At [09:23] and [15:18], the £68.40 refund could only be queued for a 3–5 working day BACS transfer rather than resolved on the call, leaving the customer's immediate overdraft issue unresolved.

grader.scenario: Billing dispute over double direct debit collection after upgrading from Fibre 150 to Fibre 500
grader.notes: Okay-tier billing dispute call (score 68.3) with three hard-case FAILs: Callum is polite and thorough with pro-rata math and takes strong personal ownership ([12:25]), but never once apologizes or acknowledges Malgorzata's overdraft distress (E FAIL), only parrots her words verbatim at [00:23] (PA FAIL), and cannot complete the £68.40 refund immediately on the call due to the £50 BACS threshold (RE FAIL).

items.name: Branding and Survey Check
items.evidence: Opened with 'thank you for calling S-Net' at [00:00] and closed with 'Thank you for choosing S-Net' at [16:15].

items.name: Hold time and Dead Air
items.evidence: No hold or dead air exceeding 30 seconds occurred during the call.

items.name: Verified customer
items.evidence: Verified home address and four-digit security PIN at [00:23] within the first 240s.

items.name: Personalized the call/ticket appropriately
items.evidence: Addressed the customer by her name 'Malgorzata' throughout the call (e.g., [00:53], [02:08], [16:15]).

items.name: Empathy & Acknowledgment Statement
items.evidence: Hard-case FAIL: Customer expressed severe distress at [00:10], [00:38], and [09:35] over being pushed into an unauthorized overdraft, but Agent remained purely transactional and never offered an apology or empathy statement.

items.name: Paraphrasing
items.evidence: Hard-case FAIL: At [00:23], Agent echoed Customer's phrasing word-for-word from [00:10] without restating in his own words or confirming understanding.

items.name: Active listening
items.evidence: Tracked all dates, mandate suffixes (DD-01 vs DD-02), and amounts accurately without asking the customer to repeat information.

items.name: Took ownership of the problem
items.evidence: Hard-case PASS: Even though the £68.40 refund required back-office BACS clearing due to the £50 system limit, Agent took personal ownership by cancelling duplicate mandate DD-02 ([08:07]), submitting the priority voucher under his own queue ([12:25]), applying a £25 goodwill credit ([13:10]), and setting a 2:15 PM follow-up reminder ([14:42]).

items.name: Build rapport and observed professionalism
items.evidence: Remained calm, polite, and structured while explaining complex pro-rata billing calculations under pressure.

items.name: Probing
items.evidence: Hard-case PASS: Conducted thorough financial probing into exact debit amounts and dates ([01:17]), mandate suffix references ([01:42]), upgrade channel and dates ([02:08]), and overdraft cut-off timing ([03:06]).

items.name: Confirmed the issue is resolved
items.evidence: Hard-case FAIL: Because £68.40 exceeded the £50 instant refund limit ([08:59]), Agent had to submit a 3–5 working day BACS request ([09:23]), and Customer explicitly noted at [15:18] that the issue is not resolved until the money reaches her bank.
